threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it ‘the tube’ instead of ‘the Underground’ like a true local. It’s a dead giveaway.
I saw a guy serenading a pigeon on the 133 last night; the bird looked genuinely confused. Only in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid ride a unicycle past the Döner shop while their grandma argued with the butcher about the best meat for Kebab. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a bar that offers ping pong tournaments while serving craft beer brewed on-site—tucked behind a graffiti-covered wall.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know to avoid BART delays by taking the bus, even if it’s labeled the most delayed. We’ve got our strategies.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where a guy serenaded the whole ride with a ukulele. Not sure if it made the delays better or worse, but we were all smiling.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's just about Gaudí and bars, but on a Sunday morning, the real vibe is families at the plaça and kids chasing pigeons.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their over-excitement at finding a 'hidden' tapas bar that everyone in Gràcia has been to at least twice.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Overground is just fancy for a train. Wait till you see rush hour on a Tuesday.
Last night on the 59, a guy sang a whole Adele song, and the bus clapped when he finished. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy playing the saxophone in the U-Bahn while a toddler danced around him, the whole carriage just smiled. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that serves vegan currywurst—I've seen locals debate it like it's a gourmet dish!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they instinctively avoid the BART platform on Fridays. No one who really lives here goes near that chaos when the brakes go out.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 in rush hour, packed as ever. If you listen closely, you can hear the bus driver's playlist through the loudspeakers—today was classic '90s hip-hop. Instant mood lift.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think our plaça is just for picnics. It’s actually our stage—every weekend, local bands play, and it’s packed with real-life conversations, not just selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with paella customs—ordering it for lunch like it's a regular dish, when locals save it for Sunday.
